correctness.rationale: Frozen mathematics: for an outsider in a clique the closed trace consists of all codewords in that clique and its selected mate, if any. For ordinary location, two empty columns are forbidden; with at most one empty column, the same-clique traces are distinct, and cross-clique equality would require both cliques to have at most one codeword, impossible for n≥4. An empty column requires both cliques to be represented. The solid condition allows precisely the exceptional single-empty, all-other-double configurations, or fully occupied columns except the 2n singleton transversals with one selected vertex on one side. The single-deletion tests for these two families and their all-set counts check out. `python /workspace/reproductions/check_discrete_claims.py 3` compared all six original formulas against literal neighborhoods for n=4,5,6. Repaired mathematics: self-location forbids an empty column, whose trace contains only vertices from one clique and whose identifying intersection would contain that entire clique. An outsider with its selected mate needs at least two selected vertices in its own clique: zero gives only the mate's neighborhood, one leaves an additional vertex on the other side, and two distinct own-side neighbors eliminate all extra vertices. Thus count fully occupied columns and remove disjoint low-shore counts (n+1)z^n+nz^(n+1) for each shore. A double column allows a deletion on the shore with at least three selected vertices (total at least n+1≥5); all feasible singleton transversals are minimal, giving (2^n−2n−2)z^n. Self-location implies outsider antichain. Crown self-location forces a full shore or one doubly omitted column; in the latter case the prism condition fails. The shared sets consist of a full shore and at least two selected vertices on the other shore. Inclusion–exclusion over the full shores proves the shared polynomial. Ran `python /workspace/repairs/3/verify.py`: literal checks of all 5376 subsets in each graph for n=4,5,6 agree with the repaired enumerators and the solid family identity. The exact proofs cover all n≥4; the finite checks do not.

evidence: Earlier crown solid cases are no overlapping omissions except 2n singleton failures, or one matched pair omitted with all other vertices chosen. Complementary trace antichains then transfer this entire code family, hence transfer one-deletion minimality too. Crown self sets instead require a full shore or single matched omission.

Neither a minimum of n in the prism nor a full classification of locating-total or distance-two sets shows that prism identifying intersections against all vertices are singletons. The repaired claim supplies that exact criterion and uses it to count the joint self family.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The solid results are credited as implied by prior work. The new self counts require a structural prism fact not obtained just by applying the prior crown self count, by reversing a trace inclusion, or by specializing a scalar bound. The shared polynomial is a corollary of that prism result and the credited crown classification.

evidence: The earlier 2026-10-13 crown work 60cce5e52da9 gives the exact all-code solid and self classifications. For an outsider, the prism and crown closed traces are complements in C. Incomparability with at least two outsiders rules out both empty and full traces, and with at most one outsider domination is automatic in these nonisolated graphs. The solid families therefore coincide on the same vertex subsets, including their inclusion-minimal sets.

The crown self family instead allows whole shores alone and single matched omissions. Neither is prism self-locating. Conversely, a balanced singleton transversal without a whole shore works in the prism only.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complementation transfers precisely the outsider antichain test, making the frozen solid enumerator prior coverage and its minimal spectrum a direct consequence of the known family. Self-location tests intersections against selected vertices as well; the crown and prism self families are not equivalent. The common subfamily requires the new prism test.

value.rationale: The surviving complete invariant distinguishes two effects of graph complementation under natural locating criteria: the solid code families are identical, while self-location has different minimal patterns in the two graphs. The exact prism polynomial, minimal-support classification, and shared-code polynomial identify the size and structure of the self-locating families with more information than the already-known minimum n. Value attaches to that structural remainder, not re-enumeration of the inherited solid family.
